LAGORI: SEVEN STONES

Experience the legendary traditional Indian street sport Pittu reimagined for modern virtual reality.

PRACTICE ARENA

Hone your physical coordination, throw accuracy, and dodging reflexes in structured modes before competitive play.

PLAY SAFELY

IMPORTANT AR/VR INSTRUCTIONS

Because Lagori requires real spatial movements (reaching, stacking, ducking, throwing):

  • Clear at least 2x2 meters of real floor space before starting.
  • Ensure no physical furniture, walls, pets, or people are near.
  • Stay centered within the yellow play boundary ring.
  • If physical discomfort or motion sickness occurs, stop immediately.

CONTROLLER CONFIGURATION

META QUEST 3 CONTROLLERS

Grab / Hold Stone: Aim controller pointer at a stone and hold down Trigger. Drag to move, release trigger to place.
Throwing Ball: Squeeze trigger to pick up the ball, swing controller physically, and release trigger at the arc to throw.
Movement: Left controller Thumbstick to walk inside the open field.
Snap Turning: Right controller Thumbstick (flick left/right) to rotate the view by 45 degrees comfort-style.

SYNCHRONIZED KEYBOARD CONTROLS

Movement: Use W, A, S, D or Arrow keys.
Snap Turning: Press Q to turn 45° left, E to turn 45° right (E also releases anything you're carrying — see below).
Grab Ball (Near): Stand near the ball and press Spacebar.
Charge & Throw Ball: Hold down Spacebar to charge throw velocity, release Spacebar to throw directly towards camera direction.

MOUSE CONTROLS (Desktop, non-VR)

Pick Up (Ball or Stone): Left-click once on the ball or a loose stone — no need to hold the button down, it stays carried in front of your camera.
Aim & Charge Throw: While carrying the ball, look toward your target — throw power builds automatically the longer you carry it (up to 1.2s).
Release / Throw / Place: Press E to let go — throws the ball, or places a carried stone if you're lined up with the pedestal.

TOUCH CONTROLS (Phones & Tablets)

Move: Drag the joystick (bottom-left) — the further you push, the faster you walk.
Look: Drag on the empty right side of the screen.
Pick: Grab the nearest ball or loose stone in reach, or whatever is under the centre dot.
Throw: Hold to charge, release to throw.
Drop / Plant: Drop what you carry, or plant a carried stone onto the tower when you face it.

CULTURAL KNOWLEDGE

What is Lagori?

Lagori (also called Pittu, Seven Stones, or Lingorchya) is an ancient street sport originating in India, dating back over 5,000 years. It is mentioned in classical Sanskrit texts including the Bhagavata Purana, where Lord Krishna is described playing the game with friends.

It remains a shared childhood memory across South Asia, representing teamwork, spatial strategy, physical agility, and simple outdoor joy.

Traditional Gameplay

The game is played between two teams: the Strikers and the Defenders. Strikers attempt to hit a tower of seven flat stones with a ball. Once the tower falls, they must quickly reconstruct it from bottom-to-top while the defenders throw the ball at them. If a striker is hit before completion, the team is out!

Physicality & Modern Decay

Unlike screen-based games, traditional Lagori requires rapid reflexes, lateral physical dodging, visual coordinate aiming, and spatial balance. Today, rapid urban congestion and small apartments mean green spaces for outdoor sports are disappearing. This XR game aims to preserve the raw physical motions in a safe, digital space.
